fields.position: Admit a skill before training through student mastery or successful teacher demonstrations. After training, pair the retrieval-free candidate with Base+ETG on the same probes.
fields.tradeoff: Only a verified release can archive eligible records; hybrid activation keeps retrieval. Local probes do not replace full rollouts. The CPU component executes the two gates without training.

fields.title: Omitting a record from the current window does not prove the weights can replace it
fields.body: MemPrice chooses which representations to read under a budget and utility estimate. After an external training update, ENGRAM compares a retrieval-free candidate with Base+ETG on the same probes to decide which training records may leave retrieval. The first saves window space without showing that the weights have learned the skill; the second tests local behavior without establishing end-to-end capability or total storage savings.

fields.question: If MemPrice omits a record this round, can that signal directly approve ENGRAM memory release?
fields.answer: No. MemPrice allocates representations under a budget. ENGRAM also needs current training participation, reserved probes, and a retrieval-free candidate that clears both thresholds. An archived record is not deleted from physical storage.
fields.example: Teaching example: Two correct answers out of four require retention at a strict 50% floor, even when Base+ETG got only one correct.

fields.summary: Added ENGRAM and separated admission, candidate activation, and verified memory release. Saving window space, shrinking retrieval, and reducing storage are different objectives. The full training experiment was not reproduced.
